title: The canonical morphism Spec O_{Y,y} -> Y is flat and identifies local rings
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $y\in Y$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ its local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with closed point $y'=\mathfrak m$. The *canonical morphism* $c:Y'\to Y$ is the morphism of schemes corresponding to the pair $(y,\mathrm{id}_A)$ (the identity map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to A$) under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring]: for any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ containing $y$, with $y$ the prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the natural map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is an isomorphism and $c$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\mathfrak p})\to\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq Y$, independent of $V$. Then: (1) $c(y')=y$, and the image $c(Y')$ is the set of generalizations of $y$; in particular $c(Y')\subseteq V$ for every open $V\ni y$, i.e. $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$. (2) For every $q\in Y'$ the local homomorphism $c^\sharp_q:\mathcal O_{Y,c(q)}\to\mathcal O_{Y',q}$ induced by $c$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] is an isomorphism; for $q=y'$ it is the identity of $A$ under $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}=A_{\mathfrak m}=A$. (3) Consequently $c$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. (4) For every $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ with pullback $c^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback], the map $\mathcal G_y\to(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ sending the germ of $s\in\mathcal G(V)$ to the germ at $y'$ of the image of $s$ under the unit $\mathcal G\to c_*c^*\mathcal G$ (a section of $c^*\mathcal G$ over $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$) is an isomorphism of $A$-modules (the stalk $(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ is $\mathcal G_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$ and $c^\sharp_{y'}$ is the identity). (5) For every ideal $J\subsetneq A$ (so that $A/J$ is a local ring and the quotient map is a local homomorphism), the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to Y$ induced by $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to A/J$ (the one corresponding to the pair $(y,\mathcal O_{Y,y}=A\to A/J)$ under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring]) is $c$ composed with the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to Y'$ given by the quotient map.

proof.text: For each affine neighborhood, use IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_stalk and IsLocalization.algEquiv to obtain the ring equivalence compatible with the germ algebra map. Mathlib IsAffineOpen.fromSpecStalk_eq_fromSpecStalk gives the asserted factorization and independence directly.

For the local-properties conjunction, Mathlib Scheme.fromSpecStalk_closedPoint, range_fromSpecStalk, and stalkClosedPointTo_fromSpecStalk prove the closed-point, range, and normalized identity clauses. Membership of a generalization in every open containing its specialization gives the preimage clause. Choose an affine neighborhood using isBasis_affineOpens. For its germ localization, Mathlib IsLocalization.isLocalization_isLocalization_atPrime_isLocalization identifies the localization at q as a localization of the affine ring at the contracted prime. IsLocalization.algEquiv gives the algebra equivalence. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext, AlgEquiv.commutes and Localization.localRingHom_to_map identify its underlying ring map with Localization.localRingHom. Scheme.localRingHom_comp_stalkIso transports this to an isomorphism on spectrum stalks; compose with the affine open immersion stalk isomorphism using Hom.stalkMap_comp. Finally apply Flat.of_stalkMap and RingHom.Flat.of_bijective to these isomorphisms.

At the closed point the stalk ring map is an isomorphism by the preceding clause. Restriction of scalars along its ring equivalence is an equivalence of module categories, so the unit of the extension/restriction adjunction is an isomorphism. Compose this unit with the restriction of the inverse of exists_tensorPullback_stalk_iso evaluated on G. Apply the forward stalk isomorphism to check the germ formula: its inverse cancels and its stated formula identifies the pulled-back germ with the pure tensor 1 tensor s, exactly the adjunction unit.

For J proper, Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff supplies nontriviality. IsLocalRing.of_surjective' and IsLocalHom.of_surjective applied to the quotient map give its local structures. The inverse of SpecToEquivOfLocalRing is definitionally Spec.map of the given local homomorphism followed by fromSpecStalk, so the factorization is reflexivity. IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective gives the closed immersion.

split_report.summary: Split along Schemes 01J6/02NA/01J7 (schemes.tex), the 'identifies local rings' remark in the proof of Cohomology 02OD and Sheaves 0098. Eight steps: c_V = iota_V o Spec(germ) through an affine open with R_p = O_{Y,y}; independence of V by passing to a smaller affine open; clause (1) from the prime correspondence of a localization and the topology of Spec; clause (2) by factoring the stalk map through the open immersion and Spec of the localization; c^#_{y'} is the identity, so c corresponds to (y, id_A) under 01J6; flatness (elementary: isomorphisms are flat); the pullback stalk via the existing node lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback (unit sk-thm-reduction, off route, used as a black-box tool as in four sibling p1 nodes); clause (5) by the 01J6 bijection. Four new Mathlib leaves (affine-open stalk localization, stalk maps of composites, stalk maps of Spec of a ring map, 01J6). Statement: clause (5) restricted to proper ideals J (for J = A, A/J = 0 is not local and 01J6 does not apply), 'corresponding to the identity' made explicit through the 01J6 node; mathematical content otherwise unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem fromSpecStalk_local_properties (Y : Scheme.{u}) (y : Y) : (Y.fromSpecStalk y) (closedPoint (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) = y ∧ Set.range (Y.fromSpecStalk y) = {x : Y | x ⤳ y} ∧ (∀ (V : Y.Opens), y ∈ V → (Y.fromSpecStalk y) ⁻¹ᵁ V = ⊤) ∧ (∀ q : Spec (Y.presheaf.stalk y), IsIso ((Y.fromSpecStalk y).stalkMap q)) ∧ stalkClosedPointTo (Y.fromSpecStalk y) = (Y.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq (fromSpecStalk_closedPoint (X := Y) (x := y)))).hom ∧ Flat (Y.fromSpecStalk y)
